messages:
anita: putting up a follow-up to the hosting abstraction RFC. I drew a boundary map where adapters implement runtime ops and the control plane handles catalog/routing/rollouts. Need to nail where tenant creds, metrics, and fallbacks live before we update the RFC.

sam: drop the sketch or paste a tiny example of the handshake?

anita: pasted below (lightweight). main questions inline.

anita: handshake proposal (minimal):
```
HandshakeV1 {
  handshake_version: "1",
  adapter_id: "string",
  capability_manifest: ["batching","kv_cache","max_seq_len:4096"],
  attestation: { adapter_cert, expires, sig },
}
```

anita: Q1: who resolves tenant KMS for Private? Option A: control plane mediates KMS and sends ephemeral creds to adapter. Option B: adapter performs KMS handshake locally and issues short-lived runtime token to control plane. My bias: B for isolation and zero-exit-key surface.

dmitri: +1 for B. adapter owning the KMS handshake reduces blast radius. Control plane should only get a bounded, auditable token. We also need a verification step so control plane can check the token wasn't forged.

sam: if adapter holds KMS, control plane needs attestable proof of the handshake. Suggest adding an attestation blob: {adapter_id, nonce, expiry, sig} where sig is by an adapter key provisioned via onboarding. Control plane validates sig against known adapter pubkey.

linda: that works. small point: the token the adapter returns should include a minimal usage scope: tenant_id, model_id, allowed_ops, expiry — no secrets. Control plane should never carry raw customer keys.

anita: agreed. Q2: what about error semantics and fallbacks? For example, Dedicated pool out of capacity -> control plane may want to route to Hosted. Adapters should return standardized error codes so routing logic can make deterministic decisions. Proposed set: ERR_CAPACITY, ERR_TEMP_OVERLOAD, ERR_AUTH, ERR_UNSUPPORTED_OP. Keep it small.

dmitri: add ERR_DEGRADED maybe for slow-paths where adapter is overloaded but not fully rejecting. Control plane can treat that as prefer-not-to-route unless no-other-path.

sam: good. Also need conservative backoff signals (Retry-After-ish) from adapters. We should avoid control plane retry storms. Handshake could include rate_hint fields.

linda: capability awareness is important. Adapter advertises max_batch_size, supports_streaming:bool, kv_cacheable:bool, and max_seq_len. Control plane uses that when composing routing and batching policies. Please avoid leaking internal runtime structs in the manifest; keep values typed/opaque strings where possible.

anita: agreed. Here's a sample capability_manifest JSON we could use in the handshake: 
```
{
  "capability_manifest_v": "1",
  "capabilities": [
    {"name":"batching","max_batch":64},
    {"name":"kv_cache","ttl_s":3600},
    {"name":"streaming","supported":true}
  ]
}
```

sam: another cross-cutting: token-level usage/metrics for billing. Runtime sees tokens but Private/on-prem may block outbound telemetry. Proposal: adapters emit signed aggregate counters (token_count, requests) that control plane ingests when allowed. For fully offline, we support manual reconciliation or local metrics sink.

dmitri: security appendix will require that counters are signed with adapter key and include a short monotonically-increasing nonce to prevent replay. They contain only numeric counters, no prompt text.

linda: ops note: for mitigations where customer forbids outbound, adapters should support a pluggable sink (push to local prom/pushgateway) and a periodic signed summary that the admin can export when permitted. Don't auto-send anything without opt-in.

anita: implementation plan: Sam will add an AdapterShim crate with handshake types + attestation verification helpers. ETA: prototype in two weeks. Dmitri will write the KMS/attestation appendix and threat model. ETA: 5 working days. I'll update the RFC to include: boundary diagram, capability manifest shape, error list, and telemetry constraints. ETA: 3 days.

sam: small tradeoff we discussed: centralizing KMS in control plane simplifies auditing but increases key-exit risk. We'll document both options and recommend Adapter-owned KMS for Private deployments and optional controlplane-mediated flow for hosted customers who prefer central audit.

dmitri: we should require handshake_version and capability_manifest_v in every handshake so adapters can evolve safely. Also specify a grace period policy for version bumps (backwards compatibility windows).

linda: ops-bot can you create a tracking ticket with the summary and owners?

ops-bot: Created issue INF-1567: "Adapter handshake + attestation + capability manifest" and linked this thread.

anita: tiny nit: mandate a minimal attestation format and a key rotation procedure for adapters in the onboarding docs. I'll add that to the RFC appendix.

sam: :+1: Also will add a small example of verifying adapter sig in the control plane doc

dmitri: :thumbsup:

linda: lgtm from infra/ops side. No blockers for the RFC update after we include the security appendix.

anita: cool. locking actions: anita -> RFC update, sam -> shim prototype, dmitri -> sec appendix. ping this thread with PR links. Closing for now.
